review_candidates.description: Women's College Hospital (WCH) is an academic, ambulatory care hospital in Ontario with a focus on health for women, health equity and health system solutions. If you're ready to be part of a team that is revolutionizing the future of healthcare, then you will want to join an institution where the possibilities for innovation, new discovery and system thinking are limitless. Women's College Hospital is committed to equity, quality and patient safety as key professional values and essential components of daily practice. Healthcare Revolutionized 2030 is our roadmap to the future. Our strategy is built on the pledge that the founders of our hospital made 140 years ago and reaffirms our commitment to providing equitable, accessible, best-in-class healthcare for everyone – meeting people where they are on their healthcare journey and partnering with them to reach their goals of living their healthiest lives possible. The stage has been set for Women’s to accelerate our priorities and capture the momentum to catapult our system forward to revolutionize healthcare for everyone. Applicants must reside and be legally eligible to work in Ontario. This is a Regular Full-Time position (New Position!) An exciting opportunity as a Peer Navigator within our Crossroads Clinic. Crossroads Clinic is a primary care clinic at Women’s College Hospital that provides comprehensive primary care to newly arrived refugees for their first two years in Toronto. Services are delivered through clinic sites at Women’s College Hospital and within COSTI’s Refugee Reception Centre, supporting newcomers and refugees in accessing timely, coordinated health care and community supports. The interdisciplinary team consists of family physicians, nurse practitioners, registered practical nurses, a social worker, and administrative staff. Background to Program Many refugees face challenges in navigating complex health and social service systems, given language barriers, lack of familiarity with the Canadian context, variable literacy and digital literacy skills, and obstacles related to immigration status. These newcomers benefit from additional navigational support in connecting to needed services, delivered in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner, which can contribute to improved access to care, improved access to material resources, enhanced sense of self-efficacy, and improved well-being. COSTI’s Reception Centre provides short-term housing to refugees arriving in Toronto and offers settlement services, housing navigation, and specialized programs designed to support newcomers as they transition into the community. By providing primary care services within the COSTI Reception Centre and Women’s College Hospital, the peer navigator helps improve access to coordinated health, settlement and social supports to newly arrived refugees and their families. A peer navigator has lived experience as a refugee, refugee claimant, newcomer, or immigrant and understands the challenges of navigating health care and social services in a new country. They draw on this experience, along with training and education, to help others navigate these systems and access support with sensitivity. Role The peer navigator will support patients at the Crossroads Clinic and at the COSTI Reception Centre in connecting to appropriate health, social, and community resources to enhance their overall health and well-being. Through an empowerment-oriented approach, the peer navigator will also enhance the capacity of patients to more independently navigate needed resources, contributing to their sense of self-efficacy and autonomy. The peer navigator will work within a multidisciplinary primary care team and will also collaborate with a variety of partner organizations. The peer navigator program will focus on patients who can benefit from navigational support, responding to patient needs and community services gaps. Activities and responsibilities may include, but are not limited to: Support clients in identifying individual priorities/goals while working collaboratively with the clinic’s interdisciplinary team and external partners Supports Crossroads Clinic and Costi Reception Centre patients in connecting with appropriate community resources, in collaboration with the Crossroads Clinic interdisciplinary team, etc) Support patients in attending health care and social service appointments (including phone call reminders, explaining public transportation routes, direct accompaniment to appointments, emotional support during appointments, etc) Assist patients in completing forms/applications related to social and health services in collaboration with the social worker and interdisciplinary team (may include electronic and paper forms) Support patients in accessing health care services through virtual technologies (e.g. educate patients on digital tools, help patients troubleshoot technological issues) Provide orientation regarding navigating the Canadian health care system and social services systems through both individual and group interventions, in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team Co-facilitate group educational sessions on a variety of settlement topics, with support from clinic team members and external collaborators Communicate patient concerns to relevant clinic team members and external partners to build awareness of patient needs and perspectives, as well as to advocate for patient priorities where needed Help patients gain skills, knowledge, and confidence to more independently access needed resources Support patients in developing self-advocacy skills Support patients in interpreting/understanding documents Provide emotional support and build rapport through active listening Engage in trauma-informed approaches to peer support and navigation Document patient encounters clearly and professionally as per the protocols of Women’s College Hospital Co-develop a repository of appropriate community resources responsive to patient needs in partnership with the interdisciplinary team and patients as co-collaborator. Attend internal team meetings and meetings with community and partner organizations, as necessary. As a role model and champion, you will work to identify and integrate safe, best practices into daily activities to foster the delivery of safe and exemplary care. Proficiency in additional languages commonly spoken by Crossroads Clinic patients and newcomers accessing services through the COSTI Reception Centre (e.g., Amharic, Arabic, or Tigrinya) is an asset but is not required. Lived experience as a refugee, refugee claimant, newcomer, or immigrant to Canada, with a strong understanding of the challenges associated with navigating health, settlement, and social service systems. Post-secondary degree or diploma, preferably with educational background in social/community services Prior peer support worker/peer navigator training an asset At least 2 years of work and/or volunteer experience in settlement services, social services, community work, peer support, or a related field. Relevant experience obtained either in Canada or internationally will be considered. Proficient in MS Office, word processing, and other digital communication platforms Familiarity with relevant resources for refugees and newcomers Familiarity with social, community, and health services in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) Demonstrated understanding of social determinants of health Sincere motivation to help other newcomers and a sense of compassion for others Excellent communication and active listening skills Strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to build and maintain trust Ability to work effectively independently and in a team Non-judgmental attitude and communication style Strong problem-solving skills and conflict-management skills Demonstrated commitment to working from an anti-racism and anti-oppressive approach Previous experience in group facilitation an asset Adaptive and flexible approach to work, willing and able to change to respond to evolving program and participant needs Strong time management and organizational skills This position plays a critical role in acting as an advocate for safety and will demonstrate principles, practices and processes that will optimize a safe environment for all Why Choose Us?
